topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by outlining the lecture's learning objectives and relating the concepts to histopathology practicals.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the discovery of transforming viruses led to the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to measure cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major classes of cancer gene mutations and illustrate their mechanistic and dosage effects through the Rb pathway and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics contrast sequence instability and chromosomal instability by examining how failures in DNA repair, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation impact cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited mutations accelerates tumor progression across various cancer syndromes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation with final remarks, book recommendations, and an outlook on upcoming lectures.
